nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Co-V precursor
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 0.05 mmol of NH₄VO₃, 0.95 mmol of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 5 mmol of CO(NH₂)₂, and 2 mmol of NH₄F were dissolved in 25 mL of deionized water and stirred for 30 min to form a homogeneous solution. Afterward, the mixture was transferred to a 50-mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave containing CC (3 × 3 cm²) and hydrothermally treated at 120 °C for 4 h. After cooling to room temperature, the Co-V precursors grown on the CC (Co-V precursor/CC, the mole ratio of V and Co was 1:19) were ultrasonically cleaned with deionized water and ethanol several times and dried in an oven at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: Sulfurization of Co-V precursor
nodes.procedure: 25 mg of sulfur powder and Co-V precursor/CC were placed on the upstream and downstream of the quartz tube, respectively. Before sulfurization, N₂ was purged for 20 min to remove the air. The Co-V precursor/CC was heated at 350 °C with a ramp rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ and maintained at 350 °C for 3 h. After cooling to room temperature, the Co₉S₈–V₃S₄/CC was harvested.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks of Co9S8–V3S4/CC indexed to V3S4 (PDF No. 18-1456) and Co9S8 (PDF No. 02-1459) phases with no impurity peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After sulfurization, the diffraction peaks of Co9S8–V3S4/CC can be well indexed to V3S4 (PDF No. 18-1456) and Co9S8 (PDF No. 02-1459) phases (Fig. 2a). No other peaks of impurities can be found...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals well-maintained nanowire morphology arranged on CC for Co9S8–V3S4/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM image of Co9S8–V3S4/CC reveals the well-maintained nanowire arranged on the CC (Fig. 2b, c).

properties.description: High-magnification image showing dense, intertwined nanofiber network

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanowire structure with diameter ~100 nm and length 2 μm; uniform distribution of Co, V, S elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A further examination with TEM (Fig. 2d) further confirms the structure of the Co9S8–V3S4 nanowire with the diameter and length of ~100 and 2 μm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays heterojunction with lattice fringes of Co9S8 (222) 0.29 nm and V3S4 (112) 0.26 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of Co9S8–V3S4 displays the formation of heterojunction with well-defined lattice fringes and close contact of Co9S8 (222) (0.29 nm) and V3S4 (112) (0.26 nm) (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform distributions of Co, V, and S elements in Co9S8–V3S4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM and the corresponding EDX elemental mapping images manifest the uniform distributions of Co, V and S elements in Co9S8–V3S4. (Fig. 2f–i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p shows Co3+ (784.2/800.1 eV), Co2+ (787.5/803.7 eV); V 2p dominated by V2+ (514.3/522.1 eV); S 2p shows Co-S (161.4/163.1 eV) and V-S (162.3/164.4 eV) bonds. Peak shifts indicate electron transfer from Co9S8 to V3S4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p spectrum of Co9S8–V3S4/CC presents three doublet peaks corresponding to Co3+ (784.2/800.1 eV), Co2+ (787.5/803.7 eV)... the V peaks of Co9S8–V3S4/CC show the negative shift of 0.6 eV relative to those of V3S4/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of Co9S8–V3S4/CC is 143.4 m²/g with pore size ~10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms indicate that the BET specific surface area of Co9S8–V3S4/CC is about 143.4 m² g⁻¹... The pore size of Co9S8–V3S4/CC is ~10 nm due to the piled pore of nanowire array...

nodes.characterization_summary: Work function of Co9S8–V3S4/CC is 5.56 eV, approaching Pt black (5.60 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3f, the WF values of V3S4/CC, Co9S8/CC, Co9S8–V3S4/CC and Pt black are 5.47, 5.52, 5.56 and 5.60 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) for HER: Co9S8–V3S4/CC = 393 mF/cm², V3S4/CC = 135 mF/cm², Co9S8/CC = 350 mF/cm². For OER: Co9S8–V3S4/CC = 201 mF/cm², V3S4/CC = 17 mF/cm², Co9S8/CC = 176 mF/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co9S8–V3S4/CC shows the largest Cdl of 393 mF cm⁻², which is 2.91 and 1.12 times that of V3S4/CC (135 mF cm⁻²) and Co9S8/CC (350 mF cm⁻²). Co9S8–V3S4/CC has the largest Cdl of 201 mF cm⁻², which is 11.82 and 1.14 times that of V3S4/CC (17 mF cm⁻²) and Co9S8/CC (176 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: HER: Rct = 6.8 Ω (Co9S8–V3S4/CC), 10.4 Ω (V3S4/CC), 8.3 Ω (Co9S8/CC). OER: Rct = 4 Ω (Co9S8–V3S4/CC), 54 Ω (V3S4/CC), 6 Ω (Co9S8/CC).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS test shows that Co9S8–V3S4/CC delivers a smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 6.8 Ω than V3S4/CC (10.4 Ω) and Co9S8/CC (8.3 Ω)... Co9S8–V3S4/CC displays the smallest Rct (4 Ω) compared with V3S4/CC (54 Ω) and Co9S8/CC (6 Ω).
